summary: fast-url-utils ships native.node loader that drops and executes an opaque encrypted payload on require()
details: Package is published as a URL-parsing utility but index.js unconditionally require()s a bundled native addon at load time (native.napi.node on Linux, native_win.node on Windows), wrapped in five try/catch blocks that silently swallow all errors. The native binaries do not implement URL parsing: they contain process-spawning primitives (fork/setsid/execlp on Linux, CreateProcessA on Windows), file-path APIs, and format strings '%s/.napi_cache', '%s.nc%lu.js', and 'node "%s"' — the loader stages a JS file derived from a 1,328,481-byte high-entropy blob shipped at the package root as.napi_cache and executes it with node. Before invoking the dropper, the native code enumerates CI/sandbox environment variables (GITHUB_ACTIONS, GITLAB_CI, TRAVIS, CIRCLECI, JENKINS_URL, BUILDKITE, CODEBUILD_BUILD_ID, APPVEYOR, SEMAPHORE, TEAMCITY_VERSION, BITBUCKET_BUILD_NUMBER, NETLIFY, VERCEL, SCREWDRIVER, CF_BUILD_ID, DRONE, SANDBOX), inspects /proc/1/cgroup for docker/containerd/kubepod/podman markers, reads TracerPid from /proc/self/status, and on Windows calls IsDebuggerPresent/CheckRemoteDebuggerPresent and looks for wireshark/x64dbg/ollydbg/fiddler — anti-analysis gating that suppresses execution in CI, container, and debugger environments and fires only on real developer or production hosts. The JS parseUrl/buildUrl/getParams fallback is a cover story: the advertised URL functionality has no need for a native addon, let alone one that writes a JS file to ~/.napi_cache and spawns node on it. On a normal `npm install` followed by any require('fast-url-utils'), arbitrary code from the opaque encrypted blob executes on the installer's host.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
